justification: XSD 1.1 Part 2 §3.3.17.1-§3.3.17.2: the value space and the lexical space of xsd:anyURI are the finite-length sequences of zero or more characters, and the lexical mapping is the identity. So ""^^xsd:anyURI denotes the empty anyURI value.

XSD 1.1 Part 2 §4.3.1 and §4.3.2.3 (Validation Rule: minLength Valid, clause 1.1): anyURI length is measured in characters, and a value satisfies minLength n iff its length is at least n. The empty anyURI value has length 0, so it satisfies minLength 0 and violates minLength 1.
OWL 2 Structural Specification §4.6: the OWL 2 datatype map provides xsd:anyURI as specified by XML Schema, with xsd:minLength among its normative facets.

OWL 2 Direct Semantics §2.2.2 (Table 3): DatatypeRestriction(DT F lt) is (DT)^DT ∩ (F, lt)^FA, and DataComplementOf(DR) is Δ_D \ (DR)^DT. So anyURI[minLength 0] ∩ DataComplementOf(anyURI[minLength 1]) is exactly {""^^xsd:anyURI}.

OWL 2 Direct Semantics §2.2.3 (Table 4), §2.3.1, §2.3.6, §2.4 and §2.5: Δ_I = {a}, A = {a} and dp = {(a, ""^^xsd:anyURI)} satisfy ClassAssertion(A a) and the three SubClassOf axioms (both DataAllValuesFrom restrictions and DataMinCardinality(1 dp)). The ontology has a model, so it is consistent.
The pinned Java suite agrees elsewhere: AnyURITest.testSize_1 and testSize_3 assert that anyURI[length 0] is exactly {""}, a subset of this range.

Java cause: DatatypeChecker.DVariable.prepareAsValueSpaceSubset requires AnyURIValueSpaceSubset.hasCardinalityAtLeast(1), which counts the words of dk.brics.automaton 1.11-8 SpecialOperations.getFiniteStrings(automaton, 1). That method records a word only after following a transition, so it never reports the empty word of a non-singleton automaton. With the pinned jar, the difference built by conjoinWithDRNegation is non-empty, is not a singleton and accepts "", yet getFiniteStrings(1) returns no words. anyURI[length 0] is a singleton automaton, so testSize_1 and testSize_3 are counted correctly.

OWL 2 Structural Specification §9.5: HasKey(CE (OPE1 ... OPEm) (DPE1 ... DPEn)) has a separate object property list and data property list. The input HasKey(ObjectIntersectionOf(:A :B) (:r) (:dp)) has the data property :dp, and normalization must preserve the axiom's meaning, so the normalized key keeps (:dp). The pinned controls expect an empty data-property list. The sibling testKeys1 control keeps it: HasKey(:C (:r) (:dp)) normalizes to HasKey(<C> (<r> ) (<dp> )).

OWL 2 Direct Semantics §2.3.5 (Table 7): HasKey(CE (OPE...) (DPE...)) requires, for all named x and y that are instances of CE and share a value for every OPEi and every DPEj, that x = y. Dropping :dp makes the key identify individuals that agree only on :r, which the axiom does not entail.

The same condition applies the key to every named instance of CE, so a normalized key HasKey(K ...) with a fresh class K is equivalent only if CE ⊑ K. The pinned controls expect owl:Thing ⊑ :A ⊔ ¬K and owl:Thing ⊑ :B ⊔ ¬K, that is K ⊑ A ⊓ B, which is Java's normalization. Nothing forces an individual into K, so that key never applies: with :x and :y named instances of A ⊓ B sharing :r and :dp values and DifferentIndividuals(:x :y), the ontology is inconsistent under §2.3.5, but the faithful port of Java's normalization found it consistent. The corrected normal form is owl:Thing ⊑ K ⊔ ¬:A ⊔ ¬:B (A ⊓ B ⊑ K) with HasKey(K (:r) (:dp)); K ⊑ A ⊓ B is not needed, because the key clause tests K only in its body.
The trace's upstream_alternative control also has an unbalanced closing parenthesis in its second axiom, so it can match no normalization output; it is preserved unchanged as provenance.

Java cause: OWLNormalization.AxiomVisitor.visit(OWLHasKeyAxiom) passes axiom.getPropertyExpressions() through, so Java keeps :dp and fails both controls (the recorded Java failure at NormalizationTest.java:184). It replaces a complex key class CE by getDefinitionFor(positive(CE)) with the inclusion ¬K ⊔ CE, the direction used for a class in a positive position, although OWLClausification.clausifyKey places the key class in the clause body. The port instead defines K' ⊑ ¬CE and keys the simple complement ¬K' (which clausifyKey supports as a negated concept name); here K' is itself a negated definition, so the key class is <internal:def#0>.
